_comment: ngsolve hdivdiv#7 (HDivDiv has no pointwise div(div(tau))). Verified 2026-08-03 on NGSolve 6.2.2604. ngs.div(tau) on an HDivDiv proxy is fine and has dims [2]; applying div a second time raises a plain Python Exception whose str() is exactly 'cannot form div', and it raises while BUILDING the expression -- before SymbolicBFI sees it -- so 'a += div(div(tau))*ww*dx' fails on the same message. The documented replacement (InnerProduct(tau, ww.Operator('hesse')) plus the normal-normal moment integral over dx(element_boundary=True)) assembles and, with M_nn=0 on HDivDiv, reproduces the Navier simply-supported value to 0.023%. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 sets N_DIV_OPERATORS=1, so ngs.div is applied to the HDivDiv proxy only once and the illegal second div -- the pathology -- is never taken. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 builds the expression without raising, so it removes 'divdiv_expression_raises=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear. Observed while running the control: the expectation 'cannot form div' SURVIVES, but only because the fixture's own FAIL diagnostic quotes that phrase back, and 'divdiv_bilinearform_raises=True' survives with a different message ('SymbolicBFI needs scalar-valued CoefficientFunction'); neither of those two strings can distinguish the pathology on its own. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py FIXED 2026-08-08: the expectation 'cannot form div' was a phrase this fixture writes itself on its own FAIL line -- i.e. it was satisfied exactly when NGSolve had NOT said it, and the fixture only stayed honest because that same line carries the forbidden 'FAIL:'. Replaced by divdiv_msg_says_cannot_form_div, computed from NGSolve's message. Executed: unmutated PASSED, T2_MUTATE=1 FAILED on divdiv_expression_raises=True and divdiv_msg_says_cannot_form_div=True.
